record.original_question: If X is a code and a bi-infinite word w has k disjoint X-factorizations with k <= |X| and at least one factorization non-periodic, must r(X) <= |X|-k+1?

evidence.quote: Let X be a code, and let w be a bi-infinite word. As- sume that for k<=| X|, w possesses k disjoint X-factorizations, such that at least one of them is non-periodic. Is it true that we have r(X)<=| X|- k + 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let A* denote the free monoid of finite words over A, with A^+ = A* \ {ε}. A subset X ⊆ A^+ is called a code if every word in X^+ admits a unique factorization as a concatenation of elements of X. A bi-infinite word over A is a sequence w = (a_i)_{i ∈ ℤ} with a_i ∈ A. An X-factorization of w is a strictly increasing two-way-infinite sequence of integers (i_n)_{n ∈ ℤ} such that, for every n, the block a_{i_n} a_{i_n+1} … a_{i_{n+1}-1} belongs to X. Two X-factorizations of w are called disjoint if their underlying sets of cut-points {i_n : n ∈ ℤ} are disjoint. A bi-infinite word w is periodic if there exists a nonzero integer p such that a_{i+p} = a_i for all i ∈ ℤ, and non-periodic otherwise.

The combinatorial rank r(X) of a finite set X ⊆ A^+ is defined as r(X) = min{|F| : F ⊆ A^+ and X ⊆ F^+}.

Question: Suppose X is a finite code and w is a bi-infinite word over A admitting k pairwise disjoint X-factorizations with k ≤ |X|, at least one of which corresponds to a non-periodic decomposition. Must one have
    r(X) ≤ |X| − k + 1 ?
artifact.status_search_result: The closely related defect theorem for bi-infinite words (Karhumäki–Maňuch–Plandowski, TCS 2003) establishes the case k = 2: if a non-periodic bi-infinite word has two disjoint X-factorizations, then the combinatorial rank of X is at most |X| − 1. The general statement for k ≥ 3 stated above does not appear to be confirmed or refuted in the available literature; its current status could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: A defect theorem for bi-infinite words
status_evidence.snippet: If a nonperiodic bi-infinite word has two X-factorizations, then the combinatorial rank of X is at most card(X) − 1.
status_evidence.claim: The k = 2 case of the conjectured inequality is established.

status_evidence.title: Defect Effect of Bi-infinite Words in the Two-element Case
status_evidence.snippet: Studies defect effect of bi-infinite words for two-element sets.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for small |X|, but the general k-case is not addressed.
